fields.short: Nobody knows yet. Four small trials couldn't tell whether nicotine pouches help people stop smoking or cut down. Ten more were under way in early 2025.

how: In the same survey, fewer who only vaped had strong cravings: 73 against 87 in 100.
Other surveys described in reviews agreed. Among 16- to 19-year-olds in England, 53 in 100 who vaped said they felt at least a little dependent, against 83 in 100 who smoked.
One web survey asked what people used. Bigger, more advanced vapes and liquids with more nicotine went with higher dependence scores.
Expert reviews in the US and Australia judged that vaping can lead to dependence. The US panel judged, less firmly, that the risk is lower than with smoking.

fields.but: The studies were small and lasted minutes to hours. None followed people nearby for weeks or years.
how: A US expert panel describes studies in test rooms and homes. The more people vaped, the more nicotine and tiny particles were in the air.
After short spells near vaping, body tests found no change in nicotine or other chemicals. Long, heavy vaping nearby, or living with someone who vaped, went with higher levels.
Some may be at special risk, the panel adds. It names children, pregnant women, older people and people with heart or lung disease.
A Dutch computer model of worst cases found small safety margins for some chemicals, like nicotine in a car. Its authors called the effects fairly mild.

Total 145, a little over 140.

fields.short: Nobody knows yet. Vaping exposes people to far less of many smoke chemicals than smoking. But the famous 95% less harmful figure is disputed.
how: A US expert panel looked at people who fully switched from smoking. In all but one study, they did better on short-term lung, heart and mouth checks.
A review for the UK government stated the figure in 2015. It says the figure still broadly fits the short and medium term.
Critics say the figure began as the views of 12 people at one meeting in 2013. They quote its paper on a lack of hard evidence for most harms.
An Australian review compares vaping mainly with no nicotine at all. Compared that way, the UK review found harmful exposure similar or higher.

Points 1 and 2 unchanged; same number and order. Advice risk: 'people who fully switched ... did better' could read as advice to switch to vaping.

fields.short: Right afterwards, it seems to. In trials, people rated their urge to smoke lower after short exercise, mostly walking or cycling, than after sitting still.

lines.reason: Short dropped 'mostly': the exercise was mostly walking or cycling, and three trials used muscle-tensing exercise. Rest accurate (one rating, people knew, authors' own trials). Advice risk: lower craving after walking or cycling could read as a tip to exercise when craving.

fields.short: For some symptoms, it seems so. All 9 trials that reported on grumpiness found less of it with nicotine gum, inhalers or tablets than with a dummy.
how: Overall discomfort was lower in 6 of 7 trials that reported it, and anxiety in 3 of 4. Results were mixed for restlessness, poor focus, sleep and hunger.
Cravings were lower in all 4 trials of the inhaler or tablet, but in only 3 of the 7 gum trials.
The trials came out between 1984 and 2000. Nothing is known past the first week, and lozenges, patches and nasal sprays weren't covered.
